decisive_moments.reason: Con directly identifies the central burden: showing autonomy matters more, rather than merely showing that adaptation can help. It also explains how shared sequencing and continuity can protect access without requiring rigid teaching methods.

Pro offers a coherent account of how teacher judgment may support durable understanding and motivation, but largely asserts that it is the more decisive factor rather than comparing its benefits against standards’ protections.

Con reinforces that the balance may differ by subject and learner and that autonomy’s benefits depend on common expectations and support. This leaves the broad superiority claim insufficiently established.
